title: Watford sack Dionisi after just 18 games
summary: Watford have dismissed head coach Alessio Dionisi after 18 games, following a 4-0 loss to Sheffield United. The club has begun searching for a replacement.
body:
Watford have dismissed head coach Alessio Dionisi after 18 games in charge, a day after the Championship side lost 4-0 to Sheffield United. The club confirmed the Italian’s departure on Sunday and said it had started the search for a replacement. Watford are 21st in the table, with four league victories under Dionisi.

Sporting director Luke Dowling thanked Dionisi and his staff for their professionalism and efforts, and wished them well. He said the club hoped to be able to announce a successor shortly. Dionisi, 46, was appointed in June after Ed Still left following three months at Vicarage Road.

Dionisi’s tenure opened with a win over Southampton, but Watford then managed only two victories in their next 12 matches in all competitions. A win against Charlton on October 17 was followed by defeats to Wolves and Norwich, before the heavy loss at Sheffield United.

Before joining Watford, Dionisi managed Italian Serie B club Empoli. He was dismissed there in March after five months, during which the team recorded five wins in 22 matches. His Watford appointment was his first managerial role outside Italy.

His departure adds to a period of frequent coaching changes at the club. Since Tom Cleverley left at the end of the 2024-25 season, Watford have appointed Ed Still, Javi Gracia, Paulo Pezzolano and Dionisi as permanent head coaches; Charlie Daniels also took charge for two matches as interim boss. Dionisi was the club’s 12th head coach, excluding interim appointments, since the end of the 2020-21 season. Watford are now seeking their 25th manager since the Pozzo family took over in 2012.

title: Bayelsa Boat Mishap: Death toll rises to 29
summary: The Bayelsa boat accident has left 29 people dead and more than 51 survivors, with recovery operations ongoing. Tinubu approved N250 million for victims’ families.
body:
The death toll from a boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has risen to 29, while more than 51 survivors have been recorded. The boat was carrying passengers to Ukubie for a burial ceremony when it capsized near Oweikorogha. Search and recovery operations are continuing, and the vessel has not yet been retrieved.

Vice President Kashim Shettima announced during a condolence visit that President Bola Tinubu had approved N250 million to support victims’ families. Tinubu also directed the Niger Delta Development Commission to procure boats to improve transport in the state’s riverine communities. Shettima said federal agencies had been asked to work with the state government on search and rescue efforts and assistance for those affected. He visited survivors receiving treatment at Bayelsa Medical University Teaching Hospital and met families of victims.

Governor Douye Diri said the state was leading the response alongside federal agencies and security services, and was covering the medical bills and feeding of survivors in hospitals. He said preliminary findings suggested the boat was not seaworthy or river-worthy and had departed from an unapproved loading point. Diri also said the state had established a commission of inquiry, and urged that its recommendations be implemented. The final casualty figure may not be known until the boat is recovered, he said, as bodies could remain trapped inside.

Diri thanked the President and Vice President for their response, while calling for federal help to speed up work on the second phase of the Nembe-Brass Road project. He also asked for collaboration on completing three senatorial roads, citing the challenges and expense of construction in Bayelsa’s riverine and deltaic terrain. Shettima said the President had directed agencies to support the affected communities, where waterways are key routes to essential services.

title: Seyi Ebenezer: Meet the banker building a global payments business from Nigeria
summary: Seyi Ebenezer moved from corporate banking to build Payaza, a Nigerian payments company operating across markets. It reported N20.16bn in 2024 revenue.
body:
After 15 years in accounting and banking, Seyi Ebenezer turned from financing other businesses to building a payments company of his own. His career included roles at KPMG, Access Bank and Keystone Bank, where he worked with companies in sectors including energy, real estate, technology and logistics. A Lagos Business School profile said he handled more than $1 billion in debt and capital transactions. He holds an MBA from Lagos Business School, an Executive MBA from Northwestern University’s Kellogg School of Management and a finance certificate from Harvard University.

Ebenezer began building Payaza Africa Limited in 2021 while still at Keystone Bank, where he remained until February 2024. The company was incorporated on March 23, 2022, and began operations in July of that year. It provides digital payment processing and mobile payment services, helping businesses collect money and make disbursements through channels including cards and bank transfers.

The early years brought regulatory delays and substantial technology costs. In an October 2025 interview, Ebenezer said the company continued investing in technology while waiting for operating licences, before it was ready to sell its services. He said Payaza reached break-even one year and nine months after beginning operations. Its audited financial statements show revenue of N20.16 billion in 2024, up from N9.47 billion in 2023. Profit after tax rose from N3.30 billion to N7.27 billion over the same period.

Payaza has since pursued growth beyond Nigeria. A 2026 credit-rating assessment said its payout infrastructure supports more than 40 currencies, while a November 2026 report described the company as operating in 31 markets. Its international relationships include Visa and Mastercard. Payaza has also used Nigeria’s commercial paper market to fund its working capital: by February 2026, it was raising funds under a N150 billion programme and had raised more than N70 billion through six series, with N32.53 billion repaid. The company is also pursuing a listing on the Nasdaq Capital Market, according to the credit-rating assessment.

title: Police arrest two nephews over killing of 70-year-old uncle in Bauchi
summary: Bauchi police arrested two men over the alleged killing of their 70-year-old uncle in Ningi. Investigators say the attack followed witchcraft accusations.
body:
Bauchi State Police Command has arrested two men over the alleged killing of their 70-year-old paternal uncle, Sa’idu Malam, in Ningi Local Government Area. Police identified the suspects as Dahiru Yakubu, 30, also known as Dangi, and Musa Alhaji Yakubu, 22. They were arrested on November 21 following an intelligence-led investigation, police spokesperson SP Nafiu Habib said.

Police received a report from a traditional ruler in Kyata village, Burra, on November 19, after Malam’s body was found beside a river. Habib said the victim, who lived in Jejin-Giwa, Kyata Ward, had marks of violence on his neck, hands and other parts of his body. He was taken to General Hospital, Burra, where a medical practitioner confirmed his death. His remains were later released to relatives for burial in accordance with Islamic rites.

According to police, preliminary investigations established that the suspects were the deceased’s nephews, sons of his younger brother. Habib said they told investigators they attacked Malam because they believed he had bewitched their wives, alleging that pregnancies had ended as a result. Police said a search of the suspects’ shelter and premises recovered a blood-stained cutlass suspected of being used in the killing.

The case remains under preliminary investigation and is expected to be transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department in Bauchi for further inquiries. Commissioner of Police Sani-Omolori Aliyu expressed condolences to the family and Jejin-Giwa community and said the command would pursue justice. He also urged the public to report grievances to the authorities rather than act on allegations or superstitious beliefs, stressing that no allegation justifies murder.

title: Bayelsa boat tragedy: NEMA deploys technical team as death toll rises
summary: NEMA has sent a technical team to support rescue efforts after a boat capsized in Bayelsa, killing 24 people. Search operations are continuing.
body:
The National Emergency Management Agency has deployed a technical team to Bayelsa State to reinforce search and rescue operations after a boat capsized in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area. Twenty-four people have died, while 24 survivors have been rescued. The search was still under way when the agency announced the figures on Saturday.

The accident occurred on Friday, November 20, 2026, at a river junction between Oweikorogha and Otuan communities. The boat was carrying passengers from Ayama to Ukubie for a burial ceremony when it capsized.

Of those rescued, 19 were taken to Ayama Clinic. Five others, who sustained injuries of varying severity, were transferred to Family Care Hospital in Yenagoa for treatment.

NEMA said its South-South Zonal Directorate had been activated earlier, and an emergency response team had been mobilised from its Port Harcourt Operations Office. The agency is coordinating with the Bayelsa State Emergency Management Agency, the Nigerian Red Cross Society, the Nigeria Police Force, the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, local divers and other responders.

Governor Douye Diri visited the scene, expressed grief over the deaths and offered condolences to the victims’ families. He also commended responders for their work and continued efforts to locate possible survivors in difficult riverine terrain. NEMA said it would continue working with relevant authorities to coordinate the operation.

title: JUST IN: 10 police vans deployed as Jimmy Odukoya attends service
summary: Ten police vans and more than 15 officers were deployed at Fountain of Life Church as Jimmy Odukoya attended Sunday service amid a leadership dispute.
body:
Ten police patrol vans and more than 15 officers were stationed around the Fountain of Life Church headquarters in Ilupeju, Lagos, on Sunday as the church’s leadership dispute continued. Worshippers underwent security checks at the entrance, including searches of bags and pockets and requests to remove metal objects before entering the auditorium.

Jimmy Odukoya attended the service and was warmly welcomed by the congregation. He told worshippers he had heard about an interim court order but had not been formally served. The order restrains him from presenting himself as the church’s senior pastor and spiritual head, and from interfering with its governance, administration and activities. The reported terms do not bar him from attending services.

The service departed from the church’s usual Sunday programme. Odukoya said there would be no regular sermon, as Bishop Mike Okonkwo, founder and presiding bishop of The Redeemed Evangelical Mission, had preached earlier. Odukoya told the congregation the remaining programme would include praise, dancing and offerings. The service was still underway when the report was filed and was expected to end at about 11:30 a.m. It was unclear whether Okonkwo’s attendance was connected to the dispute.

The court order followed a decision by a group of trustees to withdraw its recognition of Odukoya and appoint Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader. The trustees cited a purported December 2021 succession video in which the late church founder, Taiwo Odukoya, named Adekunle Areogun as his preferred successor and assigned Jimmy Odukoya roles relating to administration and the youth church.

Odukoya and supporters of his leadership have rejected the trustees’ position, arguing that his appointment as senior pastor in September 2023 was valid under the church’s constitution. He has filed a suit at the Federal High Court in Lagos challenging his removal and seeking to invalidate resolutions made by those opposing his leadership. Sunday’s gathering was the first service at the headquarters since the interim court order.

title: Multi-Trex pre-tax loss rises 79% to N1.03 billion in FY2026 despite revenue surge
summary: Multi-Trex Integrated Foods’ FY2026 revenue climbed to N3.11bn, but higher production and administrative costs pushed its pre-tax loss to N1.03bn. Cash fell N1.75bn.
body:
Multi-Trex Integrated Foods Plc reported a pre-tax loss of N1.03 billion for the financial year ended April 30, 2026, up from N577.97 million a year earlier. Revenue rose 6,392% to N3.11 billion from N47.90 million, but the sharp increase did not translate into stronger profitability. The full-year revenue came from local sales of cocoa beans, compared with N38.42 million in export sales and N9.48 million in local sales in FY2025.

The company’s cost of sales climbed to N3.10 billion from N6.82 million, absorbing almost all of its revenue. Gross profit consequently fell 79.1% to N8.58 million from N41.08 million, and the gross profit margin dropped to 0.3% from 85.8%. Administrative expenses rose 28.3% to N1.17 billion, while other operating income declined to N198.13 million from N384.31 million.

Operating losses widened to N962.96 million from N485.96 million. Although interest expenses decreased to N70.60 million from N92.01 million, the reduction was not enough to prevent the pre-tax loss from increasing. Loss after tax reached N897.06 million, compared with N578.62 million in the previous year, despite a deferred tax credit of N136.50 million.

Total assets stood at N13.79 billion on April 30, down 4.5% from N14.44 billion a year earlier. Net cash from operating activities increased to N803.45 million from N475.64 million. However, capital expenditure on property, plant and equipment rose to N3.01 billion from N1.76 billion, contributing to a N2.48 billion net cash outflow from investing activities, compared with an inflow of N667.98 million in FY2025. Cash and cash equivalents declined by N1.75 billion during the year, against an increase of N114.72 million previously. The company’s shares last closed at N0.72 on November 18, 2026, and had gained 100% year to date from an opening price of N0.36.

title: ABBACARE: How Kano is expanding healthcare access for the most vulnerable
summary: Kano’s ABBACARE scheme has enrolled 28,721 people and serves 13 hospitals, targeting healthcare costs for vulnerable groups. Its lasting impact will depend on care quality and sustained funding.
body:
ABBACARE: How Kano is expanding healthcare access for the most vulnerable

Kano State’s ABBACARE Initiative provides social health insurance coverage for vulnerable groups, including pregnant women, people living with sickle cell disorder and emergency patients. Implemented by the Kano State Contributory Healthcare Management Agency (KSCHMA), the programme aims to reduce the cost barriers that can prevent people from obtaining essential care.

Figures provided for the initiative show that 28,721 people have enrolled and that services are available through 13 hospitals across the state’s three senatorial zones. The numbers indicate the reach of the programme, but do not by themselves establish whether beneficiaries consistently receive timely, quality care. That will also depend on participating hospitals’ capacity and the availability of funding to sustain coverage.

ABBACARE is among the health interventions under Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf’s administration. Another, the Gida-Gida Lafiya Project, addresses hypertension and other non-communicable diseases by distributing customised digital blood pressure monitors. The devices are intended to help beneficiaries monitor their blood pressure, identify possible risks and seek medical attention when needed. Guidance in local languages is intended to make health information more accessible in communities.

The initiatives address different but related concerns: ABBACARE is intended to ease the financial burden of treatment, while Gida-Gida Lafiya promotes monitoring and early intervention. For ABBACARE, the next steps include maintaining coordination with hospitals, monitoring service delivery and ensuring transparent management of funds. The experiences of beneficiaries, particularly those relying on the scheme for maternal care, sickle cell treatment or emergency services, will be important in assessing its performance.

State-level schemes such as ABBACARE can contribute to broader efforts to advance Universal Health Coverage, but their wider value depends on evidence of outcomes, affordability and sustainability. For Kano, progress will be measured not only by enrolment, but by whether people can obtain reliable, affordable and quality care when they need it.

title: Naija Farmed Fish campaign moves to bring locally raised catfish to more Nigerian tables
summary: Naija Farmed Fish will promote locally raised catfish through consumer education and food events in five cities. The campaign aims to grow demand and support aquaculture businesses.
body:
A new consumer campaign, Naija Farmed Fish, aims to make Nigerian farm-raised catfish a more familiar and frequent choice for households. The initiative features the product brand Naija Catfish and the platform “It’s Catfish O’Clock,” which encourages people to enjoy catfish beyond traditional meals and occasions.

The campaign comes amid a gap between Nigeria’s fish consumption and domestic production. Figures attributed to the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations put annual consumption at about 3.6 million metric tonnes, compared with estimated domestic production of 1.2–1.4 million metric tonnes. Nigeria is also recognised as the world’s largest producer of African catfish, providing a base for efforts to expand the market for locally raised fish.

Campaign activities are planned for Lagos, Abuja, Ibadan, Enugu and Port Harcourt. They will include media engagement, consumer education, culinary storytelling and in-person experiences. The initiative also plans to address questions about farm-raised fish, including nutrition, handling and preparation, and to highlight participants across the supply chain, from farmers and feed producers to processors, traders, food vendors and restaurants.

Aquaculture specialist Sofolabi Sofela said that increasing production needs to be matched by more consumers choosing locally produced fish. The campaign’s stated aim is to help create stronger markets and business opportunities throughout the value chain. Research and interventions in Nigeria’s catfish sector have pointed to potential productivity gains from improved farm management, training and data-led practices, but sustained production growth also depends on viable markets and consumer demand.

title: ‘I Struggled To Come Out, Lost My Sister, Other Relatives,’ Bayelsa Boat Accident Survivor
summary: A Bayelsa boat survivor says she struggled to escape the capsized vessel and lost relatives and neighbours. The accident has killed 23 people.
body:
Survivor recounts struggle to escape Bayelsa boat capsize

A woman who survived a boat accident in Bayelsa State’s Southern Ijaw Local Government Area says she struggled to escape after the vessel overturned and trapped passengers beneath it. She said several of her relatives and neighbours died, including her elder sister, her sister’s son and his wife, and a neighbour and the neighbour’s son. She told Governor Douye Diri that none of their bodies had been recovered.

The boat was carrying mourners from Ayama Community to Ukubie for a burial ceremony when it capsized near Oweikorogha Community, in the Ukubie area, at about 11 a.m. on Friday. The death toll has risen to 23, while 24 survivors are receiving treatment in hospitals.

The Bayelsa State Police Command said preliminary findings indicated that the boat developed a mechanical fault while travelling along the waterways. A survivor also alleged that the wooden passenger vessel, commonly called a “love boat”, was overloaded with passengers and belongings. The circumstances of the accident are expected to be investigated by the state government.

Diri has visited the scene. The state government has warned boat operators against overloading, reckless navigation and travelling without life jackets, and urged them to follow waterway safety rules. President Bola Tinubu expressed condolences to victims’ families and directed federal disaster response agencies to support rescue and recovery work. He also directed that Saturday’s presidential campaign rally in Ibadan be held without much fanfare in honour of those who died.

title: 2027: Obi Nigeria’s only hope, says NDC chairman
summary: NDC chairman Moses Cleopas called Peter Obi Nigeria’s only hope, citing insecurity and economic hardship. He said the 2027 vote should assess Tinubu’s record.
body:
National Democratic Congress chairman Moses Cleopas has called the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, “the only hope” for Nigeria, citing worsening insecurity, economic hardship and a declining standard of living. Cleopas spoke on Saturday at a celebration of his 57th birthday in Yenagoa, Bayelsa State. NDC publicity secretary Osa Director disclosed his remarks in a statement made available to journalists in Abuja.

With the 2027 presidential election approaching, Cleopas said voters should use the contest to assess the performance of President Bola Tinubu’s administration. He argued that the decision should be based on the government’s record rather than political sentiment or party loyalty, describing the election as a referendum on whether the administration deserves another term.

Cleopas said a second-term mandate should depend on demonstrable performance, adding that voters could renew a government’s mandate if it had done well or reject it if it had not. He also urged Nigerians to examine presidential contenders’ credentials, competence and understanding of policy before deciding whom to support.

He encouraged voters to consider candidates’ records and their ability to identify the country’s challenges and propose solutions. Religious considerations and party affiliations, he said, should not outweigh those assessments.

title: Bayelsa Boat Tragedy: Death toll rises to 26
summary: The death toll from a boat capsizing in Bayelsa’s Southern Ijaw area has risen to 26. Search and recovery work continued as officials visited the scene.
body:
The death toll from a boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has risen to 26, as search and recovery operations continued into Sunday. Governor Douye Diri and his deputy visited the scene on Saturday to assess the response, while grieving relatives gathered at the Ayama waterfront.

The wooden passenger boat was travelling from Ayama to Ukubie for a burial ceremony when it capsized at about 11 a.m. on Friday, on the waterway between Oweikorogha and Otuan. The vessel was reportedly overcrowded and developed a mechanical fault during the journey.

The police initially reported four bodies recovered and 24 survivors rescued on Friday. By Saturday night, local divers and marine police had recovered 22 more bodies, bringing the death toll to 26. Nineteen survivors received treatment at Ayama Clinic, while five injured passengers were transferred to a hospital in Yenagoa. Recovery efforts were due to resume on Sunday, with divers also setting nets along the Oporoma waterways to catch bodies that may have drifted away.

A source close to the Southern Ijaw council chairman said the boat was old and not seaworthy, and that passengers had not been provided with life vests despite previous safety warnings. The council plans to enforce an order to apprehend and prosecute people who breach safety laws. The vessel’s manager was taken into custody for investigation, while the operator reportedly fled.

The Bayelsa government said it was supporting search-and-rescue operations and would assist emergency responders until they concluded. It warned operators against overloading, reckless navigation, speeding, travelling without life jackets, night journeys and operating in unfavourable weather. Community leaders have called for stricter checks on vessel seaworthiness and compliance with life-vest requirements.

title: Niger village attack sparks deadly reprisals
summary: A dawn assault in Niger State reportedly killed at least 11 people and triggered reprisal attacks on Fulani residents and refugees. Casualty totals remain unclear.
body:
Suspected terrorists attacked Lumman-Ba’are village in Niger State’s Borgu Local Government Area at about 5 a.m. on Saturday, reportedly killing at least 11 people. The dead included the village head, his wife and children. Residents said the attackers also set houses ablaze, abducted people and stole cattle. The Niger State Police Command confirmed an attack in the village; its spokesperson said police had received a report that about five people were killed and that joint security teams were deployed to pursue the suspected attackers.

A separate attack was reported in Gada-Oli at about 2 p.m., while residents were observing afternoon prayers. The number of people killed there was not specified. Residents fled both communities, and reports said worshippers were fired on during morning prayers and the village head’s palace was burned.

The initial attacks were followed by violence against Fulani residents and people displaced to nearby communities. Eyewitnesses said Kambari militias carried out reprisal attacks in Wawa, Gada Oli, Tunga Ibrahim and other villages where Fulani people lived or had sought refuge. Two witnesses estimated that about 20 bodies were in Wawa, but the overall death toll from the reprisals remains unclear. Witnesses also said the attacks lasted roughly an hour and that security personnel were not present in Wawa. Sources linked the violence there to the withdrawal of mobile police officers who had been deployed about two months earlier.

The communities have faced rising tensions amid repeated attacks attributed to a Boko Haram offshoot. Some local residents have alleged that Fulani people assisted the insurgents, a claim that has intensified hostility between the groups. Kambari militias have previously targeted Fulani residents after attacks on villages including Pisa, Kaduna Daji and Kabe, forcing many to seek safety in towns and neighbouring Kebbi State. The latest killings add to a series of attacks on rural communities in Niger State, where previous raids have killed and abducted residents, destroyed property and driven people from their homes.

title: Mexico captures drug kingpin on FBI’s most wanted list
summary: Mexico’s military says it captured Fausto Isidro Meza, a U.S. most-wanted fugitive, in a Sinaloa raid. Two associates were also detained.
body:
Mexico’s military said Saturday it had captured Fausto Isidro Meza, known as “Chapo Isidro,” during a special forces operation in Sinaloa state. The raid took place Friday night and also resulted in the capture of two other leaders of the group, including Meza’s second-in-command and a man the military identified as a financial operator.

A firefight broke out between military personnel and gang members in the town of Guasave during the operation. Local media reported that the clash caused panic in the surrounding area, including at a professional baseball game.

The military described Meza as the alleged leader of the Beltran Leyva gang, which it said is allied with one of two rival factions in the Sinaloa cartel. The three men were flown to Mexico City aboard a Mexican Air Force aircraft to be placed in the custody of prosecutorial authorities, the military said.

Meza faces criminal charges in Mexico and the United States. The FBI had included him on its list of 10 most-wanted fugitives and offered a $5 million reward for information leading to his arrest. An FBI bulletin, using the name Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores, says his group is responsible for importing large quantities of heroin, methamphetamine, cocaine, fentanyl and marijuana into the United States.

title: A gathering for peace that began with a funeral
summary: A peace assembly in Katsina went ahead five days after cleric Sheikh Yahaya Masussuka was killed. Speakers urged tolerance, justice and calm as police investigated.
body:
A gathering planned to promote peace and security in Nigeria proceeded at Muhammadu Dikko Stadium in Katsina five days after cleric Sheikh Yahaya Masussuka was killed. His name remained on the programme as host, with a 20-minute address scheduled for 11.50 a.m. Participants cheered when he was mentioned. He was also due to receive a Peace Ambassador honour, which organisers affirmed posthumously; his eldest son was designated to accept the certificate for the family.

The assembly followed a crowded funeral the previous day, attended by religious scholars, traditional leaders and mourners who had travelled to Katsina. The Saturday event had been prepared before Masussuka’s death and brought together Muslim representatives from different traditions alongside Christian leaders. Former Sports Minister Solomon Dalung said organisers had initially planned to hold it in Jos but moved it to Katsina because of insecurity.

Speakers addressed disagreements over Masussuka’s religious teachings while calling for peaceful coexistence. Sheikh Nuru Khalid said he had differed with Masussuka on some interpretations but valued him as a person committed to peace. Other scholars urged people to resolve disputes through debate rather than force. Christian cleric Golu Jan Silas recalled Masussuka’s visit to his community in Plateau State and said the cleric had promoted coexistence there. Dalung called on followers to forgive, while representatives speaking on Masussuka’s behalf urged them to avoid violence, insults and retaliation.

Gunmen killed Masussuka and his companion in Dutsin-Ma on 26 October, according to the account of the attack. The Katsina State Police Command said two armed men on a motorcycle carried out the shooting and announced an investigation. At the time of the gathering, police had not publicly identified the attackers or announced investigative findings. Ansaru claimed responsibility in videos, but those claims had not been independently established, and no evidence linked the killing to the religious disputes. Speakers called for those responsible to face justice and urged the authorities to be allowed to investigate.

title: Tinubu Mourns Bayelsa Boat Victims, Orders Rescue Agencies To Recover Bodies
summary: Four people died when a boat carrying funeral-goers capsized in Bayelsa. Tinubu ordered federal rescue agencies to assist as the search continued.
body:
President Bola Tinubu has mourned four people who died when a boat carrying scores of passengers capsized near Ukubie in Bayelsa State’s Southern Ijaw Local Government Area. The passengers were travelling to a funeral in the community on Friday, November 20, 2026. Some people were rescued, while others remained missing as search and rescue operations continued that day.

The Bayelsa State Police Command said the boat was travelling from Ayama community to Ukubie for a burial ceremony when it capsized at about 11 a.m. A preliminary police report indicated that the vessel had developed a mechanical problem while navigating the waterways.

Tinubu said he was deeply saddened by the incident and had directed relevant federal disaster response agencies to work together on recovery and rescue efforts. He expressed sympathy to the families of those affected, the Bayelsa State government and residents, and singled out Governor Duoye Diri in his condolences.

The president also directed that a presidential campaign rally scheduled for Ibadan, Oyo State, on Saturday, November 21, be held without much fanfare in honour of those who died and in sympathy with their families. He prayed for the deceased and for comfort for their relatives.

title: How I spent years in asylum camp before success in Europe – Nigerian bizman
summary: Nigerian entrepreneur Jeffrey Ekhator says he spent years in a Dutch asylum camp before building businesses in Europe. He also contested a municipal election in 2022.
body:
Jeffrey Ekhator, founder and group chief executive of Jeffangs Global Trade and Investment, says his business life began in childhood, selling goods for his mother in Benin City, Edo State. After secondary school, he worked at a filling station and later left Nigeria for France during the June 12 crisis. He moved on to the Netherlands, where he applied for political asylum because he could not study without legal documentation. He says he spent years in an asylum camp before receiving permission to stay.

Ekhator then attended integration school, college and a two-year car business programme. He says he could not complete the programme’s diploma requirements because he was unable to secure an internship. While studying at university, he worked evenings at McDonald’s and, in 2004, opened an African goods shop with his wife. The shop was destroyed by a fire just before its planned opening. Ekhator says authorities investigated but did not have enough evidence to make an arrest. He viewed the incident, and the lack of insurance compensation, as part of the discrimination he faced as a Black business owner.

After losing his investment and owing suppliers, Ekhator continued working and saving. He says an older Moroccan shopkeeper he met in Rotterdam offered to sell him a store for €25,000, payable in monthly instalments. Ekhator accepted the terms, refitted the shop with African products and drinks, and repaid the debt within a year. He later expanded into a second shop, a nightclub, a restaurant, a supermarket and a salon. His businesses import goods from several countries, including Nigeria, Cameroon, Uganda, the United States, the United Kingdom and China.

Ekhator also entered local politics, contesting a municipal election in 2022. He says he won but gave up his position in favour of a Ghanaian woman who had placed sixth. He described the campaign as a way to encourage Nigerians and other Africans to take part in local decision-making. Looking back on his progress, he points to focus, honesty and hard work as principles that have sustained him.

title: Nearly 600 women killed in South Africa in three months
summary: South Africa recorded 581 women killed from July to September, including 131 in Gauteng. Police have arrested eight suspects in a series of killings in Ekurhuleni.
body:
South Africa recorded 581 women killed between July and September, according to crime statistics released by the South African Police Service on Friday. About 131 of the victims were in Gauteng, the province that includes Johannesburg.

The figures cover a period when 13 women were murdered in Ekurhuleni, a municipality east of Johannesburg, and their bodies were left in public spaces. Victims were found in Kempton Park, Tembisa, Boksburg, Olifantsfontein and Springs. Several were partially naked and had visible bruises or other injuries. Gauteng police said on Thursday that eight suspects had been arrested.

In a separate attack in the Free State on Wednesday, five women and a toddler were killed in the township of Botshabelo. Police said three masked men entered a house looking for its owner. When they found he was not there, the men allegedly forced their way inside and opened fire on those present.

The killings form part of a wider crisis of violence against women in South Africa. A substantial proportion of women who are killed are murdered by current or former intimate partners, rather than by strangers. Police Minister Firoz Cachalia has called for greater efforts to protect women and children from violence.

The country also faces persistently high levels of homicide and gun violence. Two separate mass shootings last week killed 17 people, while another 27 people were killed in separate attacks. From April to June, South Africa recorded about 5,427 homicides, mostly in poor districts, an average of nearly 60 a day.

title: Rema Releases Seven-Track EP ‘E-Mortal Boy’, Features Wizkid On First Collaboration
summary: Rema’s seven-track EP, ‘E-Mortal Boy’, includes his first official collaboration with Wizkid. The 22-minute release also features BNYX, Theodora and Kah-Lo.
body:
Nigerian singer Rema has released ‘E-Mortal Boy’, a seven-track, 22-minute EP and his first extended play since ‘Ravage’ in 2023. Also styled as EMB, the project was released on Friday through Mavin Global Holdings and Jonzing World Entertainment, with distribution involving Interscope/Universal Music Group. It combines five new songs with two previously released singles, ‘Oh No’ and ‘TEA’.

The opening track, ‘Feel Alright’, features Wizkid and marks the first official musical collaboration between the two artists. The song focuses on romantic attraction and a lover’s desires. Thisizlondon and AoD produced the track, and both performers are credited as songwriters. The pairing also marks Rema’s first official track with any of the Nigerian artists commonly grouped as the “Big Three”: Wizkid, Davido and Burna Boy.

The EP’s other tracks bring together a range of collaborators and influences. ‘TANZANIA’ features American producer BNYX and draws on Bollywood-inspired sounds, while ‘SUGA’, with French-Congolese singer Theodora, incorporates grunge influences. The closing track, ‘Bang Bang’, features Nigerian-American singer Kah-Lo and producer Thisizlondon. The full tracklist is ‘Feel Alright’, ‘Oh No’, ‘Velvet’, ‘TANZANIA’, ‘TEA’, ‘SUGA’ and ‘Bang Bang’.

Thisizlondon, a longtime Rema collaborator who has worked on songs including ‘Calm Down’ and ‘Soundgasm’, also has production credits across the project. The release follows Rema’s 2024 second album, ‘HEIS’, which received a Grammy nomination. With ‘E-Mortal Boy’, he continues to explore different musical influences while assembling a varied group of collaborators; the Wizkid pairing is the EP’s most prominent new collaboration.

title: Grand Theft Auto VI Takes Record $3.8 bn On First day
summary: Grand Theft Auto VI generated an estimated $3.79 billion in first-day sales, nearly five times the launch-day revenue of its predecessor. The game also set a pre-release sales record.
body:
Grand Theft Auto VI generated an estimated $3.79 billion in worldwide retail sales on its first day, according to Rockstar Games. The estimate covers sales through the end of Thursday. Rockstar described the launch as the biggest for an entertainment product in history. The total is nearly five times the roughly $800 million that Grand Theft Auto V earned in its first 24 hours in 2013.

The game had sold 32.5 million units before release, a record across all platforms, the company said. It launched Thursday for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, beginning at midnight in New Zealand and becoming available in other markets as midnight arrived locally. Monitoring platform Visibrain reported that the release prompted more social media posts than this year’s World Cup.

Reviews have been highly positive. The game has a score of 99 on Metacritic, which Rockstar called the highest ever for a game. It received eight nominations for the Game Awards, scheduled for December 10. Rockstar spent more than eight years developing the title and delayed its launch twice, first from autumn 2025 and later from May 2026.

The release follows a 2022 hack in which stolen gameplay footage was posted online. The series has also faced longstanding criticism over its depiction of violence and crime, including gameplay in which players can run over pedestrians, sell drugs and shoot at police. Rockstar has no official release planned in Russia, China, Lebanon or Qatar.

title: 2027: Sowore faults NELFUND, promises non-repayable grants
summary: Omoyele Sowore says he would abolish NELFUND if elected and replace student loans with N100,000 grants each semester. He also proposed scholarships for top students.
body:
African Action Congress presidential candidate Omoyele Sowore says he would abolish the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) if elected and replace its student loan scheme with grants. Speaking during a live session on his Facebook page on Friday, he proposed payments of N100,000 per semester, saying students should be able to pursue their studies without taking on debt.

Sowore said the proposed grant would be N20,000 more per semester than the amount students currently receive through the loan arrangement. At two semesters a year, he said, students would receive N200,000 annually and N400,000 over a four-year programme. He described the payments as an investment in young Nigerians and said they would help students focus on their education.

He argued that graduates could struggle to repay loans when employment opportunities were limited. Drawing on his experience in the United States, where he said he spent 20 years, Sowore described student debt as a source of financial hardship. He also argued that borrowers were not repaying the loans currently provided in Nigeria, and said this was a reason to convert the support into grants.

Sowore also proposed scholarships for students with outstanding academic ability, including sponsorship to study abroad. He called for greater government investment in education, saying stronger support for schools was needed to reduce poverty and develop human capital. Recalling free education and community efforts to keep children in school during his childhood, he contrasted those experiences with what he described as a decline in the sector. He also cited the former standing of the University College Hospital in Ibadan and the presence of Indian and Ghanaian teachers in Nigerian secondary schools in the 1980s as examples of the country’s past capacity.

title: Tinubu appoints ex-Lagos commissioner Dabiri to NASS Service Commission
summary: President Bola Tinubu appointed Agboola Dabiri as the South-West commissioner on the National Assembly Service Commission. He succeeds Taiwo Oluwa, who left to contest an Osun seat.
body: Established under Section 157 of the 1999 Constitution, the National Assembly Service Commission is responsible for appointing, promoting and disciplining staff of the National Assembly.

title: Rivers 2027: Dumo appoints Wike’s ex-commissioner campaign strategist
summary: Dumo Lulu-Briggs has appointed former Rivers commissioner Austin Tam-George as strategy and public policy director for his 2027 campaign. The council cited his experience.
body:
Rivers State governorship candidate Dumo Lulu-Briggs has appointed Dr Austin Tam-George as Director of Strategy and Public Policy for his campaign council ahead of the 2027 election. The appointment was announced in a statement issued in Port Harcourt on Friday by the council’s media and publicity directorate.

The council said the appointment reflected its focus on strategic planning, policy development, implementation and public engagement. It said Tam-George would coordinate the campaign’s strategy, public policy framework and communications work.

Tam-George previously served as Rivers State Commissioner for Information and Communications under former Governor Nyesom Wike. The council said his experience also spans academia, government, international development, corporate affairs and strategic advisory services. He has taught at the University of Cape Town and Pan-Atlantic University, and has engaged with UNESCO and the New Partnership for Africa’s Development on areas including governance, education, youth development and institutional capacity building.

His academic and executive education includes a PhD from the University of the Witwatersrand in South Africa, the Senior Executive Fellows programme at Harvard University’s John F. Kennedy School of Government, a postdoctoral fellowship at the University of Cape Town and executive education at IESE Business School in Spain. The statement also identified him as a member of the Harvard Business Review Advisory Council.

Lulu-Briggs said he was committed to bringing accomplished professionals and experienced people into his team to contribute to changes in governance and development in Rivers State. He welcomed Tam-George as the campaign continued discussions about its agenda for the state.

title: NAFDAC Uncovers Expired Baby Diapers, Balms, Others In Lagos
summary: NAFDAC says officers found expired diapers and balms, unregistered wipes and other products in an Idumota store. The items were removed as an investigation continues.
body:
The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) says its investigation and enforcement officers found expired and unregistered products in a store at Idumota, Lagos State. The discovery was made during an operation in the area, the agency said in a post on its official X account on Friday.

The products included assorted brands of baby diapers, methylated balms, unregistered baby wipes, disposable pants and other medical products. NAFDAC said some diapers and balms were past their expiry dates, with some expired since 2022. The agency did not provide further details about the quantities or brands found.

NAFDAC said all the offending products had been removed from the store. Investigations are ongoing to establish the circumstances of their storage and how they were intended to be handled. The agency said its enforcement work is aimed at preventing expired and unregistered regulated products from reaching consumers.

The Lagos discovery followed a separate interception announced by NAFDAC at Mallam Aminu Kano International Airport. The agency said 17 cartons of suspected unregistered beverages and skin-lightening and anti-ageing injections were found concealed in a consignment declared as personal effects. The shipment lacked required import documents and was held in the custody of the Nigeria Customs Service while the importer was invited for questioning. NAFDAC cautioned that the quality and authenticity of those products had not been established.

title: Dangote supplies 31.89 million litres of petrol daily in October as imports rise 47%
summary: Dangote supplied 31.89 million litres of petrol daily in October, up 12%, while imports rose 47% to 15 million litres. Consumption increased and inventories tightened.
body:
Dangote Petroleum Refinery supplied Nigeria with an average of 31.89 million litres of petrol a day in October 2026, a 12% increase from September. At the same time, petrol imports rose 47% to 15 million litres daily, according to the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority’s October sector factsheet. Total petrol receipts climbed 21%, from 38.7 million litres per day in September to 46.9 million in October.

The refinery operated at 103.73% of its installed capacity of 650,000 barrels a day and produced an average of 48.51 million litres of petrol daily. Its operating rate was down from 105.98% in September. The regulator noted that October export shares were calculated as a proportion of production, rather than evacuation, the basis used in September’s factsheet.

Petrol consumption increased 5% month on month to 46.5 million litres a day, while diesel consumption rose 7% to 15.5 million litres. The factsheet indicated that stock sufficiency—the number of days inventories can cover consumption—declined for both fuels despite higher receipts. Crude oil deliveries to domestic refineries averaged 736,000 barrels a day, up 19% from September’s 617,000.

Modular refineries supplied an average of 680,000 litres of diesel daily, against 620,000 in September, equal to about 4.9% of the regulator’s 14-million-litre daily demand benchmark. WalterSmith, Edo Refinery, Aradel and OPAC recorded varying activity; Duport Refinery remained shut. Dangote also exported a combined 55.28 million litres of petrol, diesel and aviation fuel daily in October, compared with domestic deliveries of 43.96 million litres across those products. Botswana was reported to be seeking a fuel supply agreement with the refinery as it looks to diversify its petroleum sources.

title: ‘Bamayi’ chant sparks violence as suspected thugs attack APC convoy in Gombe
summary: Five buses carrying APC supporters were damaged and several people injured in a confrontation in Kwarge, Gombe State. No deaths were reported.
body:
Five campaign buses carrying All Progressives Congress supporters were damaged and several people injured during a confrontation in Kwarge, Balanga Local Government Area of Gombe State. No deaths were reported. The incident happened at about 5pm on Wednesday as the party’s convoy travelled from Cham to Bambam during its campaign tour of Balanga South ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The confrontation reportedly began as youths chanted “Bamayi” when the convoy approached the community. The local expression conveys rejection, disagreement or a lack of support. An eyewitness said the chanting heightened tensions and led to a clash between the youths and people accompanying the campaign team.

A source familiar with the incident said the confrontation escalated into an attack on the convoy, with some alleged attackers carrying clubs and cutlasses. Five Gombe Line buses were damaged, and several APC supporters were injured, the source said. The identities of those responsible and the precise circumstances of the violence were not clear at the time of reporting.

The incident took place on the second day of the APC’s Balanga campaign tour, following the campaign’s official launch in Bajoga, Funakaye Local Government Area, on Saturday. Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya and other party leaders had visited the palaces of the Polo of Daadiya and the Ndu of Cham to seek support. The team also travelled to Jessu-Nyuwar, Kindiyo, Mwona and Bambam for the commissioning of Local Council Development Areas. Yahaya expressed confidence in the party’s prospects, while APC officials urged residents to support its candidates in the elections.

title: Abiodun pledges to revive Iwopin Paper Mill, build Ilusin Hospital, complete Navy school in Ogun
summary: Ogun Governor Dapo Abiodun pledged to pursue Iwopin Paper Mill’s revival, build a hospital in Ilusin and complete the Navy School in Abigi. He also outlined education and infrastructure plans.
body:
Abiodun pledges Iwopin Paper Mill revival, Ilusin hospital and Navy School completion

Ogun State Governor Dapo Abiodun has pledged to explore the revival of the Iwopin Paper Mill, build a hospital in Ilusin and take over completion of a Navy School under construction in Abigi. He made the commitments on Wednesday at a meeting with party members and other stakeholders at Ilusin Community Town Hall in Ogun Waterside Local Government Area.

Abiodun said the paper mill was a Federal Government project, but his administration would seek discussions with the Federal Government about revisiting its sale and returning the facility to operation. He said reopening it could stimulate industry, create jobs and strengthen the local economy. The governor also promised a hospital in Ilusin to improve access to healthcare and said the state would complete the Navy School project in Abigi, the local government headquarters.

On education, Abiodun said his administration planned to build between 500 and 1,000 additional schools before the end of his tenure. He said more than 1,600 schools had already been rehabilitated and furnished. He attributed improved performances and awards by teachers and students in local and international competitions to sustained investment and reforms in the sector.

The governor described Ogun Waterside as an emerging investment destination, pointing to the proposed Gateway Deep Sea Port, the OgunLNG project and anticipated oil exploration as potential sources of jobs, business activity and industrial growth. He also cited more than 7,000 housing units facilitated across income categories and over 1,700 kilometres of roads built or rehabilitated across Ogun State. Among Federal Government projects and approvals he mentioned were the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, sections of the Lagos-Benin Expressway and the Ibadan-Ijebu-Ode Road, as well as dry ports approved for Kajola and Ijebu-Ode.

Abiodun urged grassroots party members to communicate government achievements to residents. Ogun APC Chairman Yemi Sanusi called on residents to support the party’s candidates, while former Deputy Governor Segun Adesegun also described the area as an emerging investment destination and urged voters to support the APC in forthcoming elections.

title: Obalende MTN bus park to open December, accommodate 1,000 buses — Wahab
summary: Lagos says the Obalende Y’ello Bus Park will open by the end of December 2026 and accommodate about 1,000 buses. Entry will be free.
body:
The Lagos State Government says the redevelopment of Obalende’s Y’ello Bus Park is expected to be completed and open for public use by the end of December 2026. MTN Nigeria is developing the facility as part of its corporate social responsibility programme, and it is designed to accommodate about 1,000 buses.

Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources Tokunbo Wahab announced the timeline during an inspection of the Obalende site and an MTN-sponsored recreational park under the Falomo bridge in Ikoyi. He said the government had agreed on a six-week completion window after discussions with transport unions, contractors and the governor’s transportation adviser. Operators are to move temporarily from the immediate construction area so work can proceed.

The park was initially given a 21-week completion target after being handed over to MTN on April 15, 2026. The September 11 deadline was missed amid heavy rainfall between June and August and operational issues involving businesses already operating at the site. Construction resumed in mid-October, and work underway by mid-November included paving, curbing and fencing. Planned features include dedicated parking and loading bays, sleeping facilities for drivers, toilets, green areas, solar lighting, electric-vehicle charging points and a recycling drop-off station.

Special Adviser on Transportation Sola Giwa said commuters and operators will not be charged to enter the terminal. The park will remain government property under the Ministry of Transportation’s supervision. Giwa said the state is working with transport unions on its use and that LASTMA will enforce rules against buses parking or picking up passengers on road corridors outside the terminal.

At Falomo, LASPARK General Manager Adetoun Popoola said the under-bridge site, previously affected by waste dumping and misuse, is being converted into a public relaxation space modelled on JJT Park in Alausa. It will be free for everyday recreation, while organisations holding formal events or competitions will pay a nominal maintenance fee.

title: Investors need swift justice, not just incentives — Elumelu
summary: Tony Elumelu urged President Bola Tinubu to speed up judicial reform, warning that delays and weak contract enforcement can deter investors. He proposed technology and court performance measures.
body:
Tony Elumelu has urged President Bola Tinubu to make judicial reform a priority, arguing that economic incentives will not be enough to attract long-term investment if commercial disputes take too long to resolve or contracts are not reliably enforced. He made the call in Abuja on Thursday while delivering the keynote address at the WOC Justice Summit, themed “The Rule of Law as a Catalyst for Private Sector Growth and Economic Transformation.”

Elumelu said investors needed fair, impartial and timely court decisions, predictable regulations and protection for contractual agreements. He warned that doubts about enforcement could prompt capital to leave, and said contracts should remain enforceable through changes in government while regulations apply equally to businesses. He cited the World Bank’s Business Ready 2025 report, which gave Nigeria scores of 63.48 out of 100 for its commercial dispute resolution regulatory framework, 24.50 for public services and 53.80 for operational efficiency. The figures point to a gap between the rules and their delivery, as well as concerns about the effectiveness of commercial justice.

He commended Tinubu’s economic measures, including removing the petrol subsidy, unifying exchange rates and enacting tax reform laws, describing them as necessary responses to longstanding economic distortions. Elumelu also acknowledged the hardship these changes have placed on ordinary Nigerians. He argued that transparent regulation in the electricity sector could help draw investment and improve power supply for businesses and public institutions, but said court delays remained a barrier to private-sector growth.

Elumelu called for technology in the judiciary and measurable performance indicators for case management and dispute resolution. He said his own investments, including a 1997 acquisition of a struggling bank with other investors, depended in part on confidence that Nigerian law would protect transactions. He also called for Africa to move beyond exporting raw materials and importing finished goods, describing African businesses as central to economic transformation. The summit marked the 75th birthday and 50-year legal career of Senior Advocate of Nigeria Wole Olanipekun, whose legal career Elumelu praised.

title: Zamfara govt inaugurates committee to review salary structure for tertiary institutions
summary: Zamfara has set up a committee to review salary and welfare concerns at state-owned tertiary institutions. It will assess costs and consult staff and management.
body:
Zamfara State has inaugurated a committee to examine the non-implementation of revised salary structures and other staff welfare concerns at state-owned tertiary institutions. Secretary to the State Government Abubakar Mohammad Nakwada, who chairs the committee, led its first meeting on Thursday in Gusau.

The committee will review relevant government circulars, assess the financial implications and funding needed to address outstanding issues, and consult stakeholders. The concerns include demands from the Forum of Zamfara State Tertiary Institutions and Zamfara State University relating to salaries, allowances and promotion benefits.

At the inauguration, Nakwada said the government wanted a comprehensive and sustainable resolution. He called for an objective review of the facts and figures, with recommendations that are fair, affordable and practical, while taking account of the state’s financial circumstances. He said the administration was committed to staff welfare, industrial harmony and improving tertiary education.

Nakwada cited the increase in the minimum wage from N7,000 to N70,000, the clearance of gratuity arrears and a new salary scale for healthcare workers as examples of the government’s worker-welfare measures. He appealed to staff and unions to be patient and give dialogue a chance, saying the committee would consider legitimate demands even if not all could be addressed at once. He also urged unions to avoid industrial action while the review is under way.

Committee members include the commissioners responsible for finance; education, science and technology; local government and chieftaincy affairs; and budget and planning. Other members represent the government’s economic and financial affairs office, the tertiary institutions’ forum, the Nigeria Labour Congress in Zamfara State and Zamfara State University. The permanent secretary of the education, science and technology ministry will serve as committee secretary.

title: 2027: Soludo presents APGA flag to Shettima for Tinubu
summary: Anambra Governor Chukwuma Soludo handed the APGA flag to Vice-President Kashim Shettima at a joint rally in Awka. APGA endorsed Tinubu for 2027.
body:
Anambra Governor Chukwuma Soludo presented the All Progressives Grand Alliance flag to Vice-President Kashim Shettima at a joint APGA-All Progressives Congress rally in Awka on Thursday. At the event, APGA formally endorsed President Bola Tinubu for the 2027 presidential election and called on party members to support his re-election bid.

The rally, held at Dr Alex Ekwueme Square and named “SoluTinubu 2027”, drew supporters of both parties, who displayed their flags and campaign materials. Soludo described the flag handover as a sign of cooperation between the parties and said they had maintained an alliance with the party at the centre since 2011.

He said the cooperation extended to elected representatives, noting that APGA lawmakers in the National Assembly work with the APC caucus. Soludo also cited the Speaker of the House of Representatives’ assessment of APGA lawmakers as cooperative. He said the partnership should continue, while candidates from both parties remained free to compete for seats in the Senate, House of Representatives and state assembly.

Under the arrangement Soludo described, lawmakers elected on one party’s ticket would work with the other party’s caucus at the relevant legislative level. He said APGA’s national leadership and wider party membership had resolved to back Tinubu and Shettima, framing the decision around national unity, progressivism and cooperative federalism. Soludo also presented the endorsement as support for a southern president completing his term before the presidency returns to the north.

title: I never planned to have two wives, 18 children – Veteran actor Oga Bello
summary: Adebayo Salami says he once wanted a quiet life with one wife but came to view his two wives and 18 children as part of his destiny.
body:
Veteran Nollywood actor Adebayo Salami, known as Oga Bello, says he did not plan to have two wives and 18 children. Speaking on the Talk to B podcast, the 73-year-old said he had originally hoped for a simple family life with one wife.

Salami said his vision was influenced by his godfather, Femi Okunnu, whose marriage and lifestyle he admired. He recalled enjoying time with his wife, including having breakfast together before he left for work, and said that was the kind of home life he had wanted.

He said his growing fame changed the course of his personal life and made it harder to maintain that arrangement. Salami also described a particularly overwhelming episode in which two women gave birth to his children in the same week. While preparing for one child’s naming ceremony, he said, he learned that another woman had also delivered a baby for him.

Salami said he has no regrets and now regards his children as part of his destiny. His family includes nine sons and nine daughters. Among them are actors Femi Adebayo, a Nollywood actor and filmmaker, and Tope Adebayo, also an actor. Salami said he had not expected some of his children to enter the entertainment industry.

title: Top Chinese bus manufacturer plans to establish plant in Nigeria
summary: Yutong plans to establish a CNG bus assembly plant in Ibadan, with 300 buses initially pledged. The programme targets fare cuts of about 40% on participating routes.
body:
President Bola Tinubu has welcomed Yutong’s plans to establish a compressed natural gas (CNG) bus assembly plant in Nigeria. The investment follows an invitation to the Chinese manufacturer to support the expansion of affordable mass transportation. An agreement with the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles is scheduled to be signed in Lagos on November 19, 2026.

Under the agreement, Yutong will supply an initial 300 CNG-powered buses. The first 100 are expected to arrive in Lagos by the end of December 2026, with subsequent vehicles to be assembled in Nigeria by YP Automobiles Bus Assembly at the former Leyland Automotive plant in Ibadan, Oyo State. The planned local assembly is intended to revive industrial capacity, reduce reliance on imported vehicles and create jobs for engineers, technicians and other workers.

The investment is linked to the National Affordable CNG Transit Programme, which is being developed with state governments. It targets fare reductions of approximately 40 per cent on participating routes, in line with the administration’s Renewed Hope Agenda 2.0 for 2027–2031. Tinubu has said that lower operating costs for CNG vehicles should result in lower passenger fares, with the programme’s success judged by the savings it delivers to Nigerians who rely on commercial transport.

The planned bus rollout comes alongside efforts to expand CNG refuelling capacity. The source material cites infrastructure work by the CNG and electric vehicle initiative, the Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund and private investors, including the deployment of mobile refuelling units and a directive for 2,000 additional refuelling units nationwide. Yutong sold 49,518 buses globally in 2025 and has experience supporting local assembly and public transport projects in several countries. Tinubu said the Nigerian investment could also support technology transfer and strengthen the country’s automotive industry.

title: Tinubu expands 2027 campaign itinerary to 19 states
summary: Tinubu’s revised 2027 campaign itinerary covers 19 states and the FCT, with 20 APC rallies scheduled through January 13. Lagos is set to host the finale.
body:
President Bola Tinubu’s planned itinerary for the 2027 presidential campaign has expanded from 12 states to 19, with the Federal Capital Territory also included. The revised All Progressives Congress calendar lists 20 rallies between October 24, 2026, and January 13, 2027. Tinubu previously said he would not be able to attend every campaign rally.

The itinerary adds Katsina, Taraba, Zamfara, Imo and Kwara, and includes Akwa Ibom, Jigawa and Kebbi, where Tinubu has already campaigned. He attended rallies in Uyo on November 6, Port Harcourt on November 7, Dutse on November 10 and Birnin Kebbi on November 17.

Upcoming stops include Katsina on December 2, Kano on December 17, Jalingo in Taraba State on December 19 and Abuja on December 21. The schedule then lists Gusau in Zamfara State on December 28 and Owerri in Imo State on December 30. Campaigning is set to resume in the new year in Yola on January 4, Sokoto on January 5 and Ilorin on January 8, followed by Asaba on January 11. Lagos is scheduled to host the final rally on January 13.

The revised calendar moves the Sokoto event from December 5 to January 5 and shifts the Lagos finale from January 9 to January 13. By region, the North-West has the most scheduled state visits, with seven. The North-East and South-South have three each, while the North-Central, South-West and South-East have two apiece.

title: FAAC disburses N2.4trn to FG, states, LGs in October
summary: FAAC allocated N2.441 trillion in October revenue to the federal, state and local governments. Statutory revenue and VAT both declined from September.
body:
The Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) distributed N2.441 trillion in October 2026 revenue among the federal, state and local governments. The allocation, agreed at a meeting in Abuja on Wednesday, comprised N1.688 trillion in distributable statutory revenue and N752.488 billion in Value Added Tax (VAT) revenue.

The committee reported that gross revenue of N3.811 trillion was available for the month. Deductions for collection costs totalled N128.797 billion, while transfers, refunds and savings amounted to N1.241 trillion. Gross statutory revenue was N2.999 trillion, down N97.323 billion from N3.096 trillion in September. Gross VAT revenue was N812.446 billion, a decrease of N4.426 billion from the previous month’s N816.872 billion.

Of the total distributable sum, the Federal Government received N856.065 billion and state governments received N809.909 billion. Local Government Councils were allocated N568.701 billion, while N206.384 billion was shared with benefiting states as derivation revenue, representing 13 per cent of mineral revenue.

Within the statutory revenue allocation, the Federal Government received N780.816 billion, states N396.040 billion and Local Government Councils N305.331 billion. The N206.384 billion derivation payment was also included in that distribution. From VAT, the Federal Government received N75.249 billion, state governments N413.868 billion and local councils N263.371 billion.

FAAC said excise duty and Common External Tariff levies rose marginally in October. Petroleum Profit Tax, Hydrocarbon Tax, petroleum royalties, import duty, Companies Income Tax, capital gains and stamp duties, VAT, mineral royalties, gas-flaring penalties and fees, and miscellaneous oil revenue all declined.

title: 2027: Tinubu expands campaign visits to 19 states, FCT
summary: Tinubu’s revised APC itinerary covers 19 states and the FCT, with 20 rally appearances planned. The schedule runs from October 2026 to January 2027.
body:
President Bola Tinubu is set to attend 20 of the All Progressives Congress’s 37 presidential campaign rallies under a revised itinerary covering 19 states and the Federal Capital Territory. The campaign programme runs from October 2026 to January 2027, and the expanded plan marks a change from the original schedule, which listed 12 states for the president’s personal appearances.

The updated itinerary, released by APC National Publicity Secretary Felix Morka, includes Katsina, Taraba, Zamfara, Imo, Kwara and Abuja, among other locations. It also incorporates Akwa Ibom, Jigawa and Kebbi, where Tinubu has already attended rallies. His appearances included events in Uyo on 6 November, Port Harcourt on 7 November, Dutse on 10 November and Birnin Kebbi on 17 November; those visits were not part of his original personal itinerary.

Further scheduled appearances include Katsina on 2 December, Kano on 17 December and Jalingo on 19 December. Tinubu is also expected in Abuja on 21 December, Gusau on 28 December and Owerri on 30 December. His January visits are due to begin in Yola on 4 January 2027, followed by Sokoto on 5 January, Ilorin on 8 January, Asaba on 11 January and Lagos on 13 January. Kaduna, Plateau, Oyo, Borno and Enugu are also on the revised list.

The timetable changes several rally dates. Bauchi’s event has moved from 29 November to 1 December, with no indication that Tinubu will attend. Sokoto has shifted from 4 December to 5 January, Asaba from 12 December to 11 January, and Lagos from 9 January to 13 January.

The North-west has the largest regional representation on the itinerary, with seven states. The North-east and South-south each have three, while the North-central, South-west and South-east each have two. At the inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Tinubu said he would not attend every rally because he did not want to abandon governance, but pledged to make time to engage Nigerians directly as party leaders campaigned across the country.

title: [VIDEO] Tinubu Can’t Alter State Police Bill, He’ll Definitely Sign It — Omole
summary: Charles Omole expects President Tinubu to sign the National Policing Bill without changes. He says the constitutional amendment must pass first.
body:
Lawyer and author Charles Omole said he does not expect President Bola Tinubu to alter the National Policing Bill sent to him by the National Assembly. Speaking on Wednesday during an interview on Politics Today, Omole said a change would send the bill back to the Senate, House of Representatives and state houses of assembly for approval. He predicted Tinubu would sign it without alteration.

Omole distinguished the constitutional amendment from the National Policing Bill, saying the amendment would allow state police to exist, while the bill sets out their structure and functions. He said the bill could not be considered until the constitutional amendment had passed.

Under the arrangement Omole described, each of Nigeria’s 36 states would have its own police service. Police in the Federal Capital Territory, however, would remain under the control of the federal police service.

Omole also said the bill recommends that states should not be able to buy arms and ammunition at will. He presented that restriction as part of the proposed framework for state policing.

title: 2026 Globe Soccer Awards: Messi, Ronaldo, Dembele, Yamal included [Full List]
summary: Lionel Messi, Cristiano Ronaldo, Kylian Mbappe, Ousmane Dembele and Lamine Yamal are among nominees for the 2026 Globe Soccer Awards. Voting runs through Nov. 30.
body:
Lionel Messi, Cristiano Ronaldo, Kylian Mbappe, Ousmane Dembele and Lamine Yamal are among the nominees for the 17th Beyond Developments Globe Soccer Awards. The shortlist was announced on Wednesday. Paris Saint-Germain and Spain are among the prominent names following their successes in the UEFA Champions League and 2026 FIFA World Cup, according to the organisers.

Dembele, who won the Best Men’s Player award last year, is again in contention for the individual prize, alongside 25 other players. Ronaldo has been shortlisted for Best Middle East Player and will seek to retain the award.

Public voting began on Wednesday across 12 categories and is scheduled to close on November 30. Fans will determine the first round, with their votes combined with those of the Globe Soccer Jury in the second round. The jury includes former football figures Marcello Lippi, Antonio Conte, Iker Casillas and Luis Figo. The ceremony is scheduled for December 28 in the United Arab Emirates. The previous edition drew more than 30 million votes from over 200 countries and territories.

title: Xi, Trump, Putin Exchange Greetings Before Historic China Summit
summary: Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin exchanged greetings in Shenzhen before their first formal trilateral summit. The agenda remained unclear.
body:
Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin exchanged greetings in Shenzhen on Wednesday, ahead of their first formal trilateral summit, scheduled for the following day. The meeting’s agenda remained uncertain, and Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said it would last no more than an hour.

Xi welcomed Trump as he arrived, meeting him at the foot of his plane’s stairs. The welcome included the two countries’ national anthems, fighter jets overhead and a red-carpet procession. The leaders later joined other attendees of the broader Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit at a dinner, where they greeted one another before a group photograph. Xi said he hoped to discuss China-US relations, Asia-Pacific cooperation and global issues with Trump.

Washington had indicated that the war in Ukraine was not expected to be discussed at the three-way meeting, but Trump later said it would be. US officials also expected discussions of the war in Iran and nuclear disarmament. A US-Russia treaty on nuclear weapons expired in February; Beijing has said the United States and Russia should reduce their much larger arsenals before China enters talks about its own.

Putin said the summit could be “highly useful” and called for dialogue amid rising military and political risks. Earlier, he said Western sanctions imposed after Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine had failed. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, also in Shenzhen, said sanctions would continue to increase while the war continued. Ukraine’s foreign minister, Andriy Sybiga, said he hoped Xi and Trump would press Russia to end it. Putin and Xi also met separately, with Xi urging closer ties between their countries.

title: Atiku Will Be On Ballot In 2027 And Will Beat Tinubu Silly — ADC
summary: The ADC says Atiku Abubakar will contest and defeat President Bola Tinubu in 2027. It is appealing a judgment affecting its leadership and candidate records.
body:
The African Democratic Congress (ADC) says Atiku Abubakar will remain its presidential candidate for the 2027 general election and defeat President Bola Tinubu. The claim was made by Phrank Shaibu, the party’s director of strategic communication, as the ADC contests a court judgment that it says has put its leadership and election preparations in legal uncertainty.

The dispute follows a November 5, 2026 judgment by Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court in Abuja in a case brought by Bala Gombe. The ADC has filed a 17-ground appeal, arguing that the trial court lacked jurisdiction, that Gombe did not have standing to bring the case, and that the court mishandled disputed evidence and issued orders that should not stand.

The party has asked the Court of Appeal to prevent the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) from changing its leadership records, Atiku’s nomination particulars or the records of its governorship candidates while the appeal is pending. The ADC argues that implementing the judgment before the appeal is decided could create uncertainty for its candidates and undermine the practical effect of a later ruling in its favour.

The party is also challenging a July 24, 2026 ruling that allowed Gombe to amend his originating summons while its objection to the trial court’s jurisdiction remained unresolved. The ADC says the amendment changed the description of parties and the capacity in which a defendant was sued without prior leave. It is asking the appellate court to set aside that order and determine the jurisdictional objection. The party says its appeals are intended to preserve its existing leadership and candidate records until the courts resolve the dispute.

title: Sunbeth completes acquisition of controlling stake in Livestock Feeds Plc
summary: Sunbeth has completed its purchase of UAC of Nigeria’s 73.29% stake in Livestock Feeds, following regulatory approvals. It plans to prioritize continuity and develop an integrated protein business.
body:
Sunbeth Treenuts and Sesame Limited, a subsidiary of Sunbeth Agro HoldCo, has completed its acquisition of UAC of Nigeria Plc’s 73.29% shareholding in Livestock Feeds Plc. The transaction followed approvals from the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission, the Securities and Exchange Commission and Nigerian Exchange Limited, making Sunbeth the company’s majority shareholder.

Sunbeth said the acquisition supports its long-term plan to develop an integrated protein business, with activity across animal nutrition and feed production, poultry and cattle production, and meat processing. The company aims to use its capabilities in agricultural sourcing, processing, manufacturing and distribution to build stronger connections across food production and support Nigeria’s livestock industry.

Livestock Feeds’ manufacturing operations, established brands and distribution network provide a base for that strategy. Sunbeth said its immediate priorities are to maintain business continuity, support operational stability and strengthen the company’s capabilities. It plans to work with Livestock Feeds’ board, management and employees, while maintaining service to customers and partners and assessing opportunities to improve efficiency and competitiveness.

Sunbeth also identified the Livestock Feeds workforce and its existing relationships with customers, distributors and suppliers as important to the company’s next phase. Its stated priorities include maintaining product quality and dependable supplies, with any operational changes introduced through a structured process.
